Council: The layered review that scored this pack: 7 Overview seats → 5 Intelligent seats → 3 Strategic seats → the Chief Decision Maker (CDM). It repeats until every seat scores ≥8 out of 10.
Residual register: The named open-item list R1–R9: things not yet proven. Each has an owner and an exit (what would clear it). Nothing on it is cleared.
Band C: Churches with weekly attendance of 250–999. MB size bands: A 2,000+, B 1,000–1,999, C 250–999, D under 250.
ICP: Ideal Customer Profile: the type of church we aim to sell to first (here, Band C).
HOLD live Core: Do not launch the Core offer to live selling yet. Value proofs V1–V4 cannot be demoed today.
PASS-with-residuals: Good enough to plan from, as long as the nine open items (R1–R9) stay named and are not presented as solved.
Explicit Unknown: We looked and could not find reliable evidence. We say so plainly instead of guessing.
Safe Switch: Proof that a church can move from its old system to MB without losing givers or data, e.g. a migration progress view. Today it is a FAIL (R1).
ASP: Average Selling Price: the typical deal price. The spoken starter floor is still open (R5).
Right to win: The reasons MB can credibly beat a rival for a deal, backed by something we can demo.
ChMS: Church Management Software: people records, giving, check-in, events, volunteers.
CDM: Chief Decision Maker: the final council seat that combines all scores and packages the result.
Confidence: High = strong public data; Medium = sound but interpolated or small sample; Low = inference or self-selected sample.
Theater: Marketing claims that cannot be checked (undated stats, superlatives like "leading").
Gift-to-books: A gift recorded to a person, matched to a bank deposit, and posted to the right fund in the accounting books, all in one vendor.
RGTP: Recurring-gift transition program: MB helps donors re-set up recurring gifts during a switch. Donors still re-enter payment details.
CM2: The coded set of 71 public reviews (rivals + legacy MB products, not current Amplify) used to learn what buyers value.
PCO: Planning Center Online, a leading ChMS rival.
JTBD: Jobs to be done: the job a church "hires" software for (e.g. make the office easy).
